# Draft:King Faisal University in Chad

King Faisal University in Chad () is an Islamic university in N'Djamena, the capital of Chad. It was founded in the 1991–1992 academic year to improve Arab Islamic education in the country.
The university offers maîtrise (one-year master's), , and doctorate degrees.
History
The university was conceived of in 1990 by Sheikh Hussein Hassan Akbar, who formed a council to discuss the feasibility of a "college of Arabic studies" in Chad. The university was recognized by the government of Chad via resolution No. 299 on 21 March 1992.  Presidential Decree No. (17/R/V/1995), issued on 30 January 1995, recognized the university as a non-profit civil institution and appointed Hussein Hassan as its president.
The first class graduated from the university in 1995. The first Diplôme d'Etudes Approfondies was granted in 1998, the first master’s degrees and "doctorates of the third degree" in 2002, and the first "state-level doctorate" in 2005.
It has been a member of the League of Islamic Universities since 1999. In 2004, it became the sub-Saharan African liaison for the Association of Islamic Universities in Cairo. It has made cooperation agreements with at least 30 Islamic universities.
Leadership
The current university president is Dr. Muhammad Buhari Hassan. The presidential councillor is Hussein Masar Hassan, who was also on the board of directors until 2021, when he was replaced with the Chadian Minister of Higher Education and Research Lydie Beassemda.
